summary: Clearwater County tower near Elk River: a 40-foot L-4 pole tower from 1934, rebuilt in 1953, destroyed in 1972. No current description found.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1972; no source describes what remains at the site.

visit.trail_note: Listed as drive-up by Idaho Fire Lookouts; no source says whether the land is open to visitors.

events.note: Tower completely rebuilt, per the association's annual report

evidence.supports: about 10 miles northeast of Elk River, Clearwater County
pole tower with L-4 cab, 1934 (40 feet)
agency is the Potlatch Timber Protective Association
tower completely rebuilt in 1953, per association annual report
evidence.quote: Boehls Butte Lookout tower was completely rebuilt this year.

evidence.supports: site listed as drive-up and destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Fire Lookout writes the association as CPTPA and Idaho Fire Lookouts writes it as CTPA. The Forest Lookouts list gives the full name, Potlatch Timber Protective Association.

notes_for_editor: Three listings agree on the 1934 tower and the 1972 destruction. The 1953 rebuild comes from a quotation of the association's annual report on the Forest Lookouts page; the report itself was not located. Elevation 3610' and Clearwater County come from the Fire Lookout listing and are now in the evidence. The record point (46.5989, -115.795) was not checked against the 'ten miles northeast of Elk River' description. By a rough estimate that point lies well southeast of Elk River, not northeast, so the coordinates may be wrong; check them before publishing. The story repeats the listing's 'ten miles northeast' wording, attributed to its sources. Idaho Fire Lookouts states that no staffing history is documented, so staffing is left out. No source describes the present site.
